one_sentence: The measurement problem's infinite regress is resolved only by a triadic unity of three distinct functions in one act, isomorphic to the Trinity.
executive_summary: This paper argues that the quantum measurement problem, formalized by von Neumann in 1932, remains unsolved because every proposed interpretation fails structurally: each either introduces a contradiction, an infinite regress, or begs the question. The core claim is that the only way to terminate the regress is through a triadic composition—three distinct functions (generation, structure, actualization) operating as a single unified act, not as a chain of observers. This structure is formally derived from the problem itself and is shown to be isomorphic to the Christian Trinity (Father, Son, Spirit). The paper concludes that this triadic unity is the minimal self-contained actualization operation, closing the regress without external watchers.
short_summary: This is a formal paper addressing the quantum measurement problem. It claims that the only structural solution to the von Neumann regress is a triadic unity of three distinct functions in one act. Key evidence includes a formal analysis showing that all alternatives (one operator, two operators, three separate operators, many-worlds, objective collapse) are self-defeating. This matters because it provides a rigorous, non-theological derivation of a Trinitarian structure from a foundational physics problem.
